experiment: Exp 6 — UCF Floor (Track B Constella Stress Test)
hypothesis: UCF minimum energy floor prevents population collapse observed in Exp 5 (drain=1.5)
null_hypothesis: UCF merely delays collapse or causes free-riding collapse

result.vs_baseline: WORSE — collapsed 2629 ticks EARLIER than Exp 5 without UCF

failure_analysis.root_cause: Population overshoot from unconditional floor support
mechanism: UCF kept all struggling agents alive long enough to reproduce
Population inflated to 848 by tick 3000 — above sustainable carrying capacity
Floor rider peak: 833 agents simultaneously on floor (nearly entire population)
Predator adaptation scaled to inflated population size
When shield adaptation maxed at tick 5000 (efficiency 0%), oversized population collapsed faster
Collapse tick 7410 — 2629 ticks EARLIER than no-UCF baseline
failure_analysis.key_metric: floor_rider_peak=833 out of 848 total population — 98% on floor simultaneously

constella_design_decision.finding: Unconditional UCF floor causes population overshoot and accelerates collapse
constella_design_decision.decision: UCF must require minimum participation/engagement to receive support. Cannot be purely existence-based.
constella_design_decision.analogy: Real UBI proposals require residency/participation — not just being alive
constella_design_decision.next_experiment: Exp 7 — UCF with minimum participation gate (agents must have reproduced within N ticks to qualify for floor support)
constella_design_decision.penumbra_connection: The participation gate IS the Penumbra zone — agents who drop below the gate enter mediation state before losing floor access entirely

track_b_implications.constella_update: UCF section must add: minimum engagement threshold for floor eligibility
track_b_implications.law_calibration: The drift from rational baseline shows participants exploit unconditional floors — law must account for this predictable behavior, not assume ideal participation
